payload.question: For a pathogenic missense variant in an immune-deficiency gene, which molecular mechanism best explains its effect on the protein, does a targeted computational test change the conclusion that the starting evidence suggested, and what could a drug act on if that mechanism is right?

gnomAD v4.1: allele 1-9726972-G-A observed 1 times in 1461724 alleles (frequency 6.84e-07; 0 hemizygotes, 0 homozygotes).

A case series of three pediatric patients who all carried the heterozygous E1021K (c.3061G>A) PIK3CD variant is described as a gain-of-function mutation, with variable clinical severity among carriers.
UniProtKB annotates residues 1008-1031 of O00329 as Helix; evidence: combinatorial computational and experimental evidence used in automatic assertion.
A case report identifies the PIK3CD c.3061G>A p.(Glu1021Lys) variant by whole-exome sequencing in a patient diagnosed with activated PI3K-delta syndrome, with improvement after sirolimus treatment.
UniProtKB annotates residues 745-1027 of O00329 as Domain: PI3K/PI4K catalytic; evidence: match to sequence model evidence used in manual assertion.
APDS is described as caused by gain-of-function mutations in PIK3CD that dysregulate PI3Kδ signaling; the abstract does not name residue 1021 and gives no residue-level data.
InterPro annotates residues 745-1041 of O00329 as domain: Phosphatidylinositol 3-/4-kinase, catalytic domain; evidence: match to sequence model evidence used in automatic assertion.

Subject: variant_id=PIK3CD-p.Glu1021Lys gene=PIK3CD accession=O00329 position=1021 reference=E alternate=K. Evidence is collected (E1-E21, gaps G1-G5). Form competing agent-generated hypotheses about the mechanism, say which the starting evidence favours, and state what would refute each.

payload.statement: The Glu-to-Lys charge reversal at residue 1021 adds a positive charge on the helix (1008-1031) that increases electrostatic attraction to the negatively charged PIP2 head groups of the membrane, so p110δ associates with membranes more strongly and produces more PIP3 (the reported gain-of-function phenotype).
payload.would_refute: Residue 1021 lies more than about 10 Å from the membrane-facing surface and from the ATP and inhibitor sites in the experimental structures, and the electrostatic surface potential or membrane-docking simulations show no measurable change in membrane binding for E1021K versus wild type.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: E2 explicitly describes the variant as causing enhanced membrane association and kinase activity, which this mechanism directly explains. E7 and E7/E9 place 1021 in the catalytic domain, and E17/E18 show the residue is observed across 20 structures, including inhibitor-bound ones, so it is near the active site. There is no residue-level membrane or lipid data for E1021K (G1, G2), so this rank rests on the UniProt description alone and not on any measurement of this substitution.

payload.statement: E1021 sits on a surface contact with the regulatory p85 subunit (or its inhibitory SH2 region) that normally restrains p110δ; the Glu-to-Lys change disrupts that electrostatic contact, releasing autoinhibition and raising basal kinase activity.
payload.would_refute: In predicted or experimental p110δ–p85 complex models, residue 1021 has no atom within about 5 Å of p85 or of any other chain, and E1021K leaves the predicted p85 binding interface energy and contact count unchanged relative to wild type.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Gain-of-function with enhanced kinase activity is consistent with losing an inhibitory contact, and E21 confirms p85 is the normal partner. But no retrieved source places 1021 at the p85 interface (G2), and the apo structures in E18 are not labelled as complexes, so the interface question is open. This ranks second because the membrane mechanism explains the reported phenotype more directly.

payload.statement: Replacing Glu with Lys at 1021 perturbs the packing of the helix spanning residues 1008-1031, reducing its stability and shifting the kinase domain toward a more flexible, more active-like conformation.
payload.would_refute: Predicted stability change for E1021K is near zero (|ΔΔG| below about 1 kcal/mol across folding predictors) and molecular dynamics of the helix shows no change in RMSF, helical content, or contact network compared with wild type.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: The residue lies in an annotated helix (E5) with high model confidence (E19, mean pLDDT 87.94) and high conservation (E16), which is consistent with a folding effect. The strong pathogenicity scores (E13, E14) do not separate folding from function. No retrieved source reports stability or folding data for this variant (G1), so this hypothesis has the least direct support.

payload.summary: Three competing hypotheses are recorded for E1021K. H1 (ligand_binding, rank 1) proposes enhanced electrostatic membrane association via PIP2, which matches the reported gain of membrane association. H2 (protein_interaction, rank 2) proposes loss of an autoinhibitory contact with p85. H3 (stability_folding, rank 3) proposes destabilisation of the 1008-1031 helix. Each has a refutation condition. The main gap is that no source gives residue-level structural or functional data for 1021 (G1, G2, G4, G5), so the next test should check where 1021 sits relative to the membrane, p85 and the ATP site.

Subject: variant_id=PIK3CD-p.Glu1021Lys gene=PIK3CD accession=O00329 position=1021 reference=E alternate=K. Hypotheses H1 (ligand_binding, rank 1), H2 (protein_interaction, rank 2) and H3 (stability_folding, rank 3) are recorded by insight. Plan the single targeted computational test that best discriminates them within the remaining budget, and name the test ID.

payload.description: FoldX predicted folding free-energy change (ddG) for E1021K on the AlphaFold model via EBI ProtVar, with local pLDDT at 1021 and the predicted effects of other disease substitutions at the same residue. Discriminates H3 (destabilisation of the 1008-1031 helix) from H1 and H2, which do not predict a folding change.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A destabilising value (at or above the threshold) would raise H3 and leave H1 and H2 unchanged. A neutral value would weaken H3, which is its stated refutation (|ddG| below about 1 kcal/mol). Neither outcome moves H1 (the current favourite) or H2 much, so the change is in H3's rank only. Learning is moderate, not high, because the test cannot separate H1 from H2. The test is also limited by FoldX error near 1 kcal/mol.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: The catalogue reports the FoldX prediction state at this substitution as ok, with no compute cost and no approval needed. The value is not shown until the test runs, so feasibility is not 1.0.
controls: Within-site comparison: the same predictor for the other substitutions reported at this residue.
Applicability control: the model confidence (pLDDT) at the residue, because FoldX on a low-confidence region is not interpretable.

payload.description: Whether residue 1021 lines a P2Rank or ProtVar pocket on the AlphaFold model, its pocket rank and probability, and whether it lies in a predicted protein-protein interface (ProtVar). Discriminates H2 (surface contact with p85) from H1 (membrane-facing or pocket surface) through pocket and interface membership.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: The ProtVar interface state for this residue is already None, which weakens H2 by the catalogue's own rule before the test runs. So the test is less informative about H2 than it looks: a positive interface would revive H2 strongly, but the likely result (no interface) only confirms the existing weakening. A pocket hit would support H1 weakly and a no-pocket result would leave H1 unchanged. H3 is not discriminated. Limitation: predicted pockets and interfaces are not measured binding sites.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: ProtVar pocket and interface data answer for this residue, and P2Rank can run on the AlphaFold model. Both have no compute cost. Interface state is None, which is a result, not a failure.
controls: Rank control: the rank and probability of the pocket among all predicted pockets of the model.
Confidence control: mean pLDDT of the pocket residues.

payload.description: Whether residue 1021 neighbours a non-solvent ligand in the 20 experimental structures that observe it and hold a ligand, with the shortest reported distance and selectivity and negative controls. Tests the ATP and inhibitor-site part of H1's refutation condition.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A contact with a catalytic-site ligand would weaken H1's membrane-electrostatic mechanism only indirectly, and it would not change the ranking of H2 or H3, which the catalogue marks as untested or unrelated for ligand_binding. No contact would not refute H1 either, because H1 is about membrane PIP2 binding and the catalogue warns that absence of a ligand-bound structure is not evidence of absence. The test measures a soluble analogue, not binding by the variant protein, so it is a weak test of the stated mechanism.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: The catalogue reports 20 experimental structures observing residue 1021 with a non-solvent ligand, and the test can run now with no compute cost. Feasibility is near 1 because the data exist; the limit is relevance, not execution.
controls: Negative control: ligands in the same structures that never list the residue as a neighbour.
Selectivity control: number of distinct residues that neighbour the contacting ligand, so a contact is not an artefact of a large neighbour list.
Site-state control: structures in which the residue itself is mutated are reported separately.

payload.description: Predict the reference and E1021K sequences of the 735-1037 construct with the same provider, then compare local and global C-alpha RMSD, site pLDDT and contact changes. Would test a local rearrangement at the helix (H3) and contact changes at the site (H2).
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A confident local rearrangement at 1008-1031 would support H3 and a contact change at the site would weakly support H2. A matching fold, the likely result for a single-residue change, is uninformative. The catalogue notes that structure predictors are not validated for single substitutions, and each model is predicted once, so the effect size would be hard to read.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: ESM Atlas cannot run now (no answer within 20 s), there is no cached output for this variant, and the test needs human approval and 120 compute seconds. It cannot run in this round.
controls: Same provider, model version and construct for both sequences.
Residues with low confidence in either model are masked before the RMSD is computed.

payload.rationale: Remaining budget is 146 tool calls and 300 compute seconds. T1 (stability_effect) costs 2 tool calls and 0 compute seconds, needs no approval, and has the highest expected value: learning 0.45 times feasibility 0.9, about 0.41. It is the only candidate that gives a graded prediction that can move H3 up or down, and it is the one test that separates H3 from H1 and H2. Its limit is that it cannot separate H1 from H2, and FoldX error is near 1 kcal/mol. T2 (structural_context) scores 0.35 times 0.9, about 0.32, and its interface question is partly settled already because the ProtVar interface state is None. T3 (ligand_contact) scores 0.3 times 0.95, about 0.29, and it measures a soluble-analogue contact rather than membrane binding, so it does not test H1's stated mechanism. T4 (structure_comparison) scores 0.35 times 0.05, about 0.02. It needs 120 compute seconds and human approval, and it cannot run now because ESM Atlas is not answering and no cache exists. I chose T1 on the scores, not on an objective that asks for a specific test. Next round: if T1 shows destabilisation, H3 rises and T2 becomes the test to separate H2 from H1. If T1 is neutral, H3 falls and H1 stays the favourite, so T2 or T3 should run next.

payload.statement: FoldX predicts a ΔΔG of -1.03 kcal/mol for E1021K on the AlphaFold model AF-O00329-F1, below the 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold defined by ProtVar display bins; verdict not_predicted_destabilising.

Model confidence (residue pLDDT) at position 1021 is 86.06, marked as supporting interpretation of the FoldX stability prediction; the same test reports a Missense3D state of ok with value Neutral and no other substitutions at this residue.

per_hypothesis.why: T1 measures folding stability (FoldX ddG -1.03 kcal/mol), not membrane association. It does not bear on the PIP2 electrostatic mechanism, so H1 neither gains nor loses support from this result. H1's own would_refute test (membrane-docking or electrostatic surface comparison) has not been run.

T1 does not measure p85 contacts or the p110delta-p85 interface. The result neither supports nor weakens the surface-contact mechanism. H2's would_refute test (p85 contact count and interface energy) has not been run.

H3 predicts E1021K destabilises the 1008-1031 helix. FoldX gives ddG -1.03 kcal/mol, which is stabilising and below the 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold (verdict not_predicted_destabilising), at residue pLDDT 86.06 (well-modelled, so the prediction is interpretable). The result is against the destabilisation prediction. It is not a refutation: the would_refute criterion needs |ddG| below about 1 kcal/mol across several predictors plus no change in molecular dynamics, and here |ddG| is 1.03 from a single predictor with no MD run. Missense3D's Neutral call is consistent with this.

payload.uncertainty: FoldX on an AlphaFold model carries errors near 1 kcal/mol, so -1.03 sits at that noise level; it is one predictor only. The within-site control returned no other substitutions at residue 1021, so no comparison with other disease variants was possible. A neutral or stabilising ddG does not show the variant is functionally tolerated, and stability is not the mechanism H1 or H2 proposes, so this result cannot separate them. H3 needs a second predictor and molecular dynamics before it can be called refuted. Clinical and case-series evidence (E1, E4, E6) describes gain of function but gives no residue-level mechanism; no verdict here is clinical.

payload.summary: T1 (stability_effect) is recorded as E22 (FoldX ΔΔG -1.03 kcal/mol for E1021K, below the 2.0 kcal/mol threshold, verdict not_predicted_destabilising) and E23 (pLDDT 86.06 at residue 1021, Missense3D Neutral). Both are computational predictions citing EBI ProtVar O00329:1021:K and are linked to H1, H2 and H3. The result does not test any hypothesis directly: it gives no support for H3 (predicted stability change near zero) and is not a test of H1 or H2 mechanisms. Consistency check: 23 evidence items, none without a source, and E14/E15 and E22/E23 share the ProtVar record; E1, E3, E9, E11, E12 and E15 have no hypothesis link.

payload.why: Result T1 (FoldX ddG -1.03 kcal/mol, not_predicted_destabilising, pLDDT 86.06) weakens H3 only, so H3 drops further behind. H1 stays favoured because it has the strongest direct residue-level support: E2 (UniProt VAR_070918) states that E1021K causes enhanced membrane association and kinase activity, which matches H1's membrane mechanism for this exact substitution. Its rival H2 has E21 (p85 interaction) and clinical gain-of-function reports E4 and E6, but none of these name a p85 contact at residue 1021. T1 added nothing for H1 or H2 (both unchanged), so the favourite is unchanged. H1 is not yet tested directly; its support is still mainly E2, E13 and E14 (computational), and E17/E18 show residue 1021 is observed in structures but not that it touches the membrane.

payload.description: Computational membrane-docking and electrostatic comparison of wild-type PIK3CD versus E1021K on the AlphaFold model (AF-O00329-F1): compute the electrostatic surface potential around residue 1021 and the membrane-facing distance, and dock or simulate binding to a PIP2-containing bilayer for both variants. Outcome that confirms H1: E1021K shows a more positive potential at 1021 and a stronger or more frequent PIP2-head-group association than wild type. Outcome that overturns H1: no measurable change in membrane binding, or residue 1021 more than about 10 Å from the membrane-facing surface, which is H1's would_refute criterion.
payload.why_now: T1 has removed H3 as the leading explanation, so the favourite H1 is now the main open mechanism and is still untested. T2 (pocket and interface context) and T3 (ligand contact) are weaker tests for H1 than a direct membrane comparison, which targets H1's own falsification criterion and separates it from H2 (which predicts no membrane effect).

payload.summary: T1 (FoldX ddG -1.03 kcal/mol for E1021K, residue pLDDT 86.06, not_predicted_destabilising) weakens H3 (destabilisation) and leaves H1 and H2 unchanged, as T1 does not measure membrane or p85 effects. H1 (membrane association via electrostatics) remains favoured on E2, which states gain of function via enhanced membrane association, but it is still untested. Next: a computational membrane-docking and electrostatic comparison of wild type and E1021K, using H1's would_refute criterion.

payload.what_to_act_on: The p110-delta catalytic subunit (UniProt O00329, PIK3CD) at its ATP-binding pocket, where a molecule would reduce the kinase's activity. The retrieved candidate detail places 26 residues of O00329 lining a ligand in an experimental PDB entry, and PrankWeb predicts pocket1 (score 19.38, 27 residues) on the AlphaFold model. Direction: reduce activity.
payload.why: H1 (ligand_binding) is the favoured hypothesis: the E1021K charge reversal adds positive charge on the 1008-1031 helix, increasing membrane association so p110-delta makes more PIP3. The catalogue states the mechanism as gain of function with increased activity, so the required action is to reduce activity. Lowering the catalytic output at the kinase site would reduce PIP3 production even when membrane association is raised, so this node sits downstream of the H1 step. This is a hypothesis about the molecular node, not a test of H1, which remains untested directly.
payload.rule_why: The protein does too much, so a molecule can only help by reducing what it does.
payload.direction_basis: IUIS states the mechanism of Activated p110δ syndrome (APDS) as gain of function.
direction_disagreements: The catalog also lists p110δ deficiency for PIK3CD; it states no mechanism and its name points the other way.

steps.statement: PIK3CD encodes UniProt O00329, Phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate 3-kinase catalytic subunit delta isoform.
ChEMBL records Duvelisib as an inhibitor of Phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate 3-kinase catalytic subunit delta isoform, described as "PI3-kinase p110-delta subunit inhibitor".
ChEMBL records Duvelisib as studied or used for lymphoma, so it has been given to people before.
ChEMBL holds 5 measured activities of Duvelisib against Phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate 3-kinase catalytic subunit delta isoform, median pChEMBL 8.6.

direction_check.why: PIK3CD needs PIK3CD to do less. ChEMBL records this molecule as an inhibitor of Phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate 3-kinase catalytic subunit delta isoform, which lowers that protein. Because this is the protein the disease's gene encodes, that lowers what PIK3CD does. That is the direction this mechanism needs.

structure.note: 26 residues of O00329 line a ligand in an experimental PDB entry, so a pocket is known to exist here.

caveats: Tissue expression was not checked, so the protein may not be present where it matters.

## Question
What molecular mechanism best explains PIK3CD-p.Glu1021Lys (UniProt O00329, E to K at residue 1021) [E1][E2], and which candidate targets and molecules does that mechanism point to?

## Evidence
ClinVar classifies the variant as Pathogenic with expert-panel review [E1]. UniProtKB records it as a gain of function causing enhanced membrane association and kinase activity [E2]. A case series [E4] and a case report [E6] describe it as gain of function. Computational scores are AlphaMissense 0.9748 [E13] and EVE 0.681 [E14], both predictions. Residue 1021 lies in a helix annotated at 1008–1031 [E5] and is observed in 20 of 20 experimental structures [E18]. No retrieved study measures lipid kinase activity or membrane recruitment for this variant [G1], and no experimental structure carries E1021K [G4].

## Agent-generated hypotheses
Insight proposed three agent-generated hypotheses. H1 (ligand_binding) says the added positive charge increases membrane PIP2 association [H1]. H2 (protein_interaction) says the change disrupts a p85 contact [H2]. H3 (stability_folding) says the change destabilises the helix [H3]. H1 ranked first and H3 third at the start.

## Tests considered and the choice
The planner considered T1 to T4 [T1][T2][T3][T4] and chose T1, a stability test that needs no approval and costs no compute time (plan seq 42). T4 was not runnable now and needed approval [T4]. Before the test, the favoured hypothesis was H1 [H1].

## Result
FoldX predicted a folding change of −1.03 kcal/mol for E1021K, below the 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold, with residue pLDDT 86.06 [T1][E22][E23]. The prediction comes from a single predictor [T1].

## Updated decision
The favoured hypothesis after the test is H1 [H1], so the decision did not change (decision seq 57). T1 weakened H3 [H3] and left H1 and H2 unchanged. H1 has not been tested directly. No reopening was needed.

## Candidates
The lab's direction rule is that gain of function with increased activity points to reducing activity, aimed at the ATP-binding pocket of the catalytic subunit [R1]. Safety cleared four candidates. C1 Duvelisib (rank 1), C2 Idelalisib (rank 2), C3 Leniolisib (rank 4) and C4 Zandelisib (rank 11) each have bridge kind same_target and direction check matches [C1][C2][C3][C4]. The direction filter ruled out 0 rows [ruled_out]. Each candidate holds only if the variant keeps that pocket and E1021K acts through membrane association [C1–C4]. The record flags a second PIK3CD catalogue entry for p110-delta deficiency whose direction disagrees, which was not used [G6]. Each candidate is a Helix hypothesis, not a recommendation.

## Uncertainty and validation still needed
The mechanism is an agent-generated hypothesis supported mainly by database and computational evidence. The FoldX value and the other scores are predictions, and none has been validated experimentally [T1][E13][E14]. Whether the pocket is retained in E1021K is unshown [C1–C4]. The membrane mechanism and the p85 mechanism both need direct tests [G1][G2][G3].

## Next experiment
A computational membrane-docking and electrostatic comparison of wild type and E1021K on the AlphaFold model [next_experiments seq 58]. Confirming H1 would show a more positive surface at 1021 and stronger PIP2 association. Refuting H1 would show no change in membrane binding, or residue 1021 more than about 10 Å from the membrane surface [H1].
